correctness.rationale: The initiating source arXiv:2203.03060 Eq. (3)-(5) has L2 diagonal triple degrees and leaf-pair entries minus half the pair codegree; with d1=2(n-1)/n and d2=3t/n both normalized matrices have trace n. Every per-triple contribution has eigenvalues 0,3/2,3/2, making L positive semidefinite. Therefore lambda2<=n/(n-1), with equality iff L=(nI-J)/(n-1). Hub-to-leaf entries uniquely force alpha=(n-2)/n, and leaf-pair entries then force a constant positive codegree mu. The converse follows from 3t=mu*C(n-1,2), yielding all off-diagonals -1/(n-1). Leaf-contrast/hub-contrast invariant subspaces give the exact two eigenvalue branches and unique optimal mixture. An explicitly supplied Fano triple list has exactly one incidence per leaf pair; t=7 compared with 35 complete triples. A freshly executed standalone checker verified 13 balanced-design cases, 7273 exhaustive subset/alpha cases at n=4..6 and exact Fano matrix identities. Finite checks are corroborative only. The proof is complete for all n>=4 and nonempty simple triple H, with alpha in [0,1].

evidence: Zhang–Lucas–Battiston 2023 results derive a known minimum-degree upper bound and report random hypergraph optimum alpha; an upper bound alone does not give equality topology.
Lucas–Cencetti–Battiston 2020 Section V.A treats a star linked by a single bridge to a clique, and states higher-order interactions there do not change lambda2.
Skardal et al. 2021 p.2 restrict to clique complexes (every triad requires all three pairwise edges) and optimize heterogeneous-frequency synchrony alignment, excluding independent star/leaf-triples.
Wang–Ji–Lü 2025 §4.1 maximizes lambda_N of a multiorder Laplacian using hyperedge contributions, distinct from maximizing lambda2 subject to a star layer.

originality.rationale: The spectral trace upper bound and complete-graph equality matrix are known graph-Laplacian facts; they are not claimed as novel. The investigated primary 2022/2023 multiorder-synchronization source explicitly provides degree-based upper bounds and observed optimum mixing but not the exact star/leaf-triad all-equality characterization and Fano sparse full-spectrum equivalence. The 2020 star-clique construction has two almost-disconnected subnetworks and differs from the present one-hub/leaf-triples hypergraph. The 2021 Skardal paper studies clique complexes and a distinct frequency-alignment eigenvalue objective. The 2025 Wang et al topology algorithm optimizes the largest eigenvalue, not lambda2. Targeted mathematical-record search found no covering claim. Residual risk: an unindexed equivalence connecting balanced designs to the normalized mixed-order Laplacian cannot be excluded.
residual_risks: An unindexed article or terminology variant might derive the same star–leaf block-design equality characterization.
The universal spectral bound is standard and explicitly excluded from the novelty claim.
The theorem concerns a hypergraph with independent pair and triple layers; not a simplicial complex or arbitrary oscillator nonlinear global stability.

value.rationale: The natural question is whether sparse nonpairwise interactions can repair the slow transverse mode of a star while keeping the normalized total coupling fixed. The exact iff block-design classification and unique alpha=(n-2)/n solve that design problem, and all pair-balanced sparse triple systems exhibit exactly the full spectrum of the dense complete system for any alpha. A seven-triple Fano plane matches thirty-five leaf triples at n=8 and doubles the star-only gap, with general n savings by a factor n-3 when Steiner systems exist. This is a motivated structural optimality and sparsification theorem, not a narrow unmotivated enumeration or a claimed novel proof of an existing trace bound.
